unavailable_fields.communication: Not applicable: single-device task (observations.json capability field 'communication' status not_applicable, reason 'single-device task'); request.json distributed_backend is null and lists exactly one device; resnet_inference.py runs one process with no process group and no NCCL init.
unavailable_fields.nccl_algorithm_protocol_channel_selectio: No NCCL collectives exist in this workload (single device), so nccl_tuning has nothing to capture; kernel entry names alone would not identify the protocol even if kernels existed.
unavailable_fields.per_collective_transfer_bytes_pcie_nvlin: No collectives to attribute; device_telemetry samples device-wide NVML PCIe rates/utilization with native windows, not per-collective bytes; PCIe/NVLink traffic must not be inferred from logical payload or memcpy sizes.
unavailable_fields.gradient_bucket_identity_and_storage_mem: inference_mode forward only; coverage.json shows 0 backward_associated_kernels and 0 autograd_ranges, so no gradient buckets or communication hooks exist; exact bucket links would require native correlation plus observed gradient-storage membership, which no available collector supplies.
unavailable_fields.synthetic_allreduce_reference_timing: collective_calibration runs a separate warmed full-world SUM allreduce at observed sizes/dtypes; with world size 1 and communication not_applicable there is no collective to calibrate, and it is a reference experiment, not a performance lower bound or critical-path estimate for this objective.
unavailable_fields.candidate_exception_and_false_return_eve: No candidate files exist yet in this first collection round; candidate_diagnostics records only exceptions (including handled ones) and False returns in supplied candidate files on the worker's current thread, so empty events would not establish which successful path executed.
unavailable_fields.per_site_numerical_error_and_first_diver: candidate_diagnostics does not compare intermediate tensors, measure per-site numerical errors, or locate the first numerical divergence, and no other available collector supplies these observations; they remain unknown. Quality is enforced by the evaluator's own full-logits assert_close (atol=rtol=1e-4) and exact top-1 checks.
unavailable_fields.additive_candidate_binding_overhead: binding_cost is not applicable before any candidate exists; it compares an additive candidate (retains all installed parent bundles and adds new ones) against a binding-only passthrough in clean AB/BA workers and reports whole-invocation cost. It will be reconsidered once such a candidate exists, including in subsequent candidate resource feedback.
unavailable_fields.clean_host_dispatch_and_binding_costs: python_runtime runs a perturbing warmed cProfile call trace; its inclusive/self times are not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations, and the images_per_second floor is enforced by the evaluator's clean sample loop (resnet_inference.py:41-48), not by perturbed profiling.
unavailable_fields.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_completion_bo: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for CPU-to-CUDA submissions only; GPU readiness and consumer completion may remain unknown. Not requested because torch coverage already associated 103/103 kernels with 0 ambiguous_forward_sequences, so no attribution or overlap question is open.
unavailable_fields.nsys_attribution_of_allocator_peak: nsys would add a second timeline without resolving the objective: attribution is already complete (coverage.json: 103 associated, 0 unassociated, 0 root_only_kernels, 0 ambiguous sequences), the eager forward uses no CUDA graphs, and after the 2 warmup forwards the PyTorch caching allocator reuses segments, so an nsys CUDA-API timeline would not expose the per-repeat torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated peak that defines the metric.

rationale: The frozen objective is the process-level PyTorch CUDA allocator peak (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated per repeat after reset_peak_memory_stats, resnet_inference.py:41-48) for one batch-32 FP32 inference_mode forward, with an images_per_second >= 0.95x-baseline floor measured by the evaluator's clean timing. The torch collector already ran and fully attributed the trace (coverage.json: cuda_kernels=103, associated_kernels=103, unassociated=0, root_only_kernels=0, backward_associated_kernels=0, autograd_ranges=0, ambiguous_forward_sequences=0), so the nsys selection criteria (open overlap, graph-tracing or attribution questions) are not met. Communication-oriented collectors are excluded on observed evidence: observations.json marks capability 'communication' not_applicable ('single-device task'), request.json has distributed_backend null and a single leased GPU, and the trace contains no NCCL kernels, no backward work and no gradient buckets. Candidate-dependent collectors (candidate_diagnostics, binding_cost) are premature because no candidate exists yet; binding_cost will be reconsidered in candidate resource feedback once an additive candidate is supplied. python_runtime and execution_timeline are excluded because profiling perturbs execution and never yields clean throughput or GPU-duration scores, and a second trace would duplicate the already-complete attribution. device_telemetry is excluded because its device-wide NVML readings (PCIe rates, utilization, memory with native windows) are not the process allocator peak and there is no communication to measure. Memory optimization therefore proceeds from the existing torch trace evidence (per-op shapes/kernel timings) plus the evaluator's own clean peak_allocated_bytes and images_per_second measurements; dimensions no actual collector can supply are recorded in unavailable_fields with observed reasons rather than requested indiscriminately.
